plan_v3_S4_amendment.reason: Same defect class as PRT v6 Part A MAJOR and CP2 v7 M3: foreign metadata reached through attribute lookup or formatting outside an origin handler. Plan v3 section 7 S4 stated the rule generally; the replacement list must cover every site below.
rules: One type-name helper: name = type.__dict__["__name__"].__get__(type(x)); use it only if type(name) is str exactly, else the fixed marker "<type-name unavailable>". Never concatenate, format or compare a str subclass taken from foreign metadata.

Exception descriptions: str(exc) only inside a BaseException guard; a failure there is retained as an origin (S2); the text is used only if type(text) is str exactly, else "<description unavailable>".
Real-type classification only: issubclass(type(exc), Exception); never isinstance on a foreign exception (isinstance consults exc.__class__ when the real type does not match).
No getattr/setattr and no __context__ read or write on foreign exceptions; attachments via the base instance dict (dict.get / dict.__setitem__).
Calls into parent-supplied objects (reader attributes and report(), CP2 log methods, callbacks) run in origin handlers: a non-Exception BaseException is retained with origin=True.
Raw parent-supplied containers are checked with exact-str keys before any set or equality comparison.

cp1_v2_sites_9f3d158b.issue: type(exc).__name__ and str(exc); guard catches Exception only; the fallback repeats the unguarded type-name lookup
kind.__name__ on a foreign value's type
type(value).__name__ on a callback return (RETURNED event)
type(value).__name__ on a detached JSON value (safe today; use the helper for uniformity)
__context__ read/write on foreign exceptions (removed in v3; the prior tuple is the retention channel)
getattr on the parent reader outside an origin handler
reader.report() BaseException propagates unretained; _why on its Exception
set(identity) == {...} on a raw parent dict without an exact-str-key check (foreign __eq__ on a hash collision)
